## Install (no npm account needed)

```bash
npm install github:auroraxo/sememe#v0.4.5
```

```js
import { decodePayload } from 'sememe';
```

The registry name is deliberately unpublished (no name squatting): the git tag is the release artifact.

## What's in v0.4.5

- **A base58 payload is a payload.** The CLI has always documented "base58 or hex" for every payload argument, but the base58 path decoded to a byte array that was not a `Buffer`, and three consumers need `Buffer` methods. So the SAME bytes behaved differently depending on how they were written — measured against the PUBLISHED v0.4.4 install (a pinned install of tag `v0.4.4`), not against a working tree:
  - `sememe decode --union <program> <base58>` failed on EVERY base58 payload with `unionDecode needs the payload bytes as a Buffer`, while the same payload as hex decoded fine. The README's own union walkthrough uses a base58 payload, so it could not run.
  - an `f64`/`f32` argument died with `slice.readDoubleLE is not a function` (measured on OpenBook v2 `stubOracleCreate`, price 1.5).
  - a `bytes` argument came out as a comma-separated byte list (`1,2,3,255`) instead of base64 (`AQID/w==`) — silent corruption, not an error.
- **The fix is in three layers.** Root cause: `decodeBase58` returns a `Buffer` (a `Buffer` IS a `Uint8Array`, so every existing caller keeps working). The codec's `Cursor` normalizes its bytes to a `Buffer` once, so the shape of the input cannot decide whether it decodes. The union path normalizes instead of refusing, and still refuses input that is not a byte array at all.
- **`test/base58-payload-bytes.test.mjs` pins the equality.** For each of the three cases, the base58 form and the hex form must produce the same instruction, the same fields and the same verdict — plus the CLI end to end. Two mutations (revert `decodeBase58`; remove the `Cursor` guard) must turn the contract red, so the guards are not decorative. Suite: 515 tests, 513 pass, 2 named-skip, 0 fail.

## Honest limits

No external users yet (0 non-owner signals), not an audit, own-host measurement. The three defects were measured against the published v0.4.4 install on this host, and the fix is verified by the suite and by a pinned-install journey against the fixture store — not by a stranger on another machine. The fix changes the shape of one internal return value (`decodeBase58` now returns a `Buffer`); `Buffer` is a `Uint8Array`, so no existing caller breaks, but a caller that asserted the exact constructor would see a difference. v0.4.4 keeps its defect (tags are immutable); its release page carries the SUPERSEDED banner pointing here.

> **SUPERSEDED — use [v0.4.5](https://github.com/auroraxo/sememe/releases/tag/v0.4.5).**
>
> Measured 2026-11-06: the base58 payload path was broken in the PUBLISHED
> v0.4.4 install — `sememe decode --union <program> <base58>` failed on every
> base58 payload with "unionDecode needs the payload bytes as a Buffer" while
> the same payload as hex decoded fine, f32/f64 arguments died with
> "slice.readDoubleLE is not a function", and a `bytes` argument came out as a
> comma-separated byte list instead of base64. The front-page pin still pointed
> at v0.4.4, so a stranger following it received a package whose own README
> walkthrough (a base58 payload) could not run. Tags are immutable, so the pin
> moved to `v0.4.5`, whose tree fixes it; the v0.4.3 release page keeps its
> banner.
>
> Measured 2026-11-05: the lock (`sememe lock` / `sememe verify`) shipped on main AFTER this tag was cut, so a stranger following the front-page pin received a package whose CLI has no lock at all — `npx sememe lock` exited 2 with the usage dump and wrote no lock file, while the README they read says the lockfile ships. Tags are immutable, so the pin moved to `v0.4.4`, whose tree carries `src/lock.mjs`; the v0.4.3 release page keeps this banner. `test/lock-journey.test.mjs` pins it: the pinned tag's documented lock journey must run verbatim from the bare install.


The registry name is deliberately unpublished (no name squatting): the git tag is the release artifact.

## What's in v0.4.4

- **The pinned install now carries the lock the README documents.** The lock shipped on main (b8465bf) hours after v0.4.3 was tagged; the front page still pointed at v0.4.3, so the copy-paste install yielded a CLI without `lock`/`verify` (both exit 2, usage dump) while the README around it announced the lockfile. This tag is cut from main, so the documented journey runs from the install: `npx sememe pull ... --store ./store` → `npx sememe lock --store ./store --out ./sememe.lock` → `npx sememe verify --store ./store --lock ./sememe.lock` (measured verbatim against live mainnet before tagging: pull slot 465799518, fingerprint `sha256:0b886e37…660f`; lock → verify, 1 pinned, 1 verified, 0 violations).
- **The lock section's fresh-machine dead end is closed.** The two documented lock commands ran against `--store /tmp/sememe-demo`, but no documented step created that store — measured verbatim: exit 1, `no sememe store at /tmp/sememe-demo`. The section now documents the store-creating `pull` BEFORE the commands that need the store, in both the clone and the install form.
- `test/lock-journey.test.mjs` pins both: L1 runs the pinned tag's own documented lock journey from the packed tarball against the committed fixture store; L2 refuses a lock section whose store-consuming command has no pull command before it; G1 guards main.

## Honest limits

No external users yet (0 non-owner signals), not an audit, own-host measurement. The journey test proves the shipped README's commands exist and run — it does not prove a stranger's success on a machine that is not this host. The lock is not a freshness check against the chain and does not cover vendored programs (System, ComputeBudget, SPL Token, Token-2022, Raydium AMM v4). `sememe gap` and `sememe pull` need `@solana/web3.js`; every other subcommand runs without it. v0.4.3 keeps its defect (tags are immutable); its release page carries the SUPERSEDED banner above.

> **SUPERSEDED — use [v0.4.4](https://github.com/auroraxo/sememe/releases/tag/v0.4.4).**
>
> Measured 2026-11-05: the lock (`sememe lock` / `sememe verify`) shipped on main AFTER this tag was cut, so a stranger following the front-page pin received a package whose CLI has no lock at all — `npx sememe lock` exited 2 with the usage dump and wrote no lock file, while the README they read says the lockfile ships. Tags are immutable, so the pin moved to `v0.4.4`, whose tree carries `src/lock.mjs`; `test/lock-journey.test.mjs` pins it: the pinned tag's documented lock journey must run verbatim from the bare install.

## What's in v0.4.2

- **The pinned tag's OWN README now runs the consumer journey.** Measured on the packed `v0.4.1` tarball (2026-11-05): the consumer section had no `pull` command, so the first decode died with `no sememe store at ./store: run "sememe pull" first`; and the only invocation form that works from an install (`npx sememe`) appeared 0 times — bare `sememe` is not on `PATH` after a plain `npm install`, and `node bin/sememe.mjs` resolves only inside a clone. `v0.4.1`'s README could not be fixed (tags are immutable), so the pin moved here, where the shipped README documents `npx sememe pull` / `npx sememe decode` verbatim.
- `test/installed-tag-journey.test.mjs` measures the PACKED TARBALL of whatever tag the README pins — the bytes a `github:#<tag>` install receives — and fails if that tag's README lacks the store-creation step or a runnable CLI form. The tag is resolved locally or fetched from origin; if it is not published, the test skips with that reason instead of measuring a different tree.
- The install pins point at `v0.4.2`, whose tree ships everything the README documents (`sememe gap`, `sememe/raydium`, `sememe/token-metadata`).

## Honest limits

No external users yet (0 non-owner signals), not an audit, own-host measurement. Instruction-data decoding is the proven path; account/event decoding is exercised by tests but not by an outside consumer. `sememe gap` and `sememe pull` need `@solana/web3.js`; every other subcommand runs without it. The journey test proves the shipped README's commands exist — it does not prove a stranger's success on a machine that is not this host.

> **SUPERSEDED — use [v0.4.2](https://github.com/auroraxo/sememe/releases/tag/v0.4.2).**
>
> Measured 2026-11-05 on the packed `v0.4.1` tarball: this tag's shipped README has no store-creation command before the decode that needs `./store`, and documents no invocation form that runs from an install (`npx sememe` appears 0 times). Tags are immutable, so the journey was repaired and re-tagged as `v0.4.2`; the README now pins `v0.4.2`.

## What's in v0.4.1

- **The README's peer-refusal claim is now true.** It said the CLI "refuses `sememe pull` without [the optional peer] ... and still runs every other subcommand" — but `sememe gap` probes the same on-chain IDL addresses, so it needs the peer too and refuses as well. Measured on the installed tree (2026-11-05): 2 of 13 subcommands need `@solana/web3.js` (`gap`, `pull`), the README named 1.
- `tools/measure-release-surface.mjs` now derives the peer-needing commands statically from the bin's import graph and fails the README when the claim and the tree disagree.
- The install pins point at `v0.4.1`, whose tree ships everything the README documents (`sememe gap`, `sememe/raydium`, `sememe/token-metadata`).

## What's in v0.4.0

- `sememe gap <program>` — classify one program's acquisition gap (pullable / no-interface-published / present-undecodable / vendored / unknown; RPC failure exits 3, never a fake absence).

- Release-surface measurement: `tools/measure-release-surface.mjs` derives the pre-fix verdict defect-by-defect from committed inputs (`research/release-surface-2026-11-05-before.json`).
